sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Haoma** ​(*haoma*) ‌— Sacred ‌Plant, ​Immortality ​· ​The pressed ​one ​— ‌belongs ​to the ​Zoroastrian ‌tradition, ​where it ‌is ​catalogued ‌under ​the domain ​"Sacred ​Plant, ​Immortality". ​The name ‌means ​"The ‌pressed ​one".

**Haoma** ‌is ​sacred ‌plant, ​immortality. The ‌name ​means ​"The ‌pressed one" ‌and ‌belongs ​to the ​zoroastrian ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores the ‌name ​as ​**Haoma** ‌and serves ​its ‌temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/haoma/). ​The ​restoration ‌needs ‌no distinctive ​letters ‌or ​diacritics its ​ASCII ‌form ‌would ‌lose, which ‌places ​the ‌name ​in Tier ​2. ​The ‌plain ​ASCII form ​*haoma* ​survives ‌as ​a modern ​convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name ‌is attested ‌in ​Avestan ​as ​**𐬵𐬀𐬊𐬨𐬀**. Etymologically ​it ​means ‌"The ​pressed one".

​The ‌ASCII ​form ‌*haoma* survives ​only ‌because ​the ​early domain-name ​system ​could ​not ‌carry diacritics; ​it ‌is ​a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ​ancient ‌spelling. The ​Unicode ​restoration ‌**Haoma** ‌recovers the ‌full ​diacritic ​detail ‌of the ​scholarly ​transliteration ‌directly ​in the ​address ‌bar. ​The ‌restoration needs ​no ​distinctive ​letters ​or diacritics ‌its ‌ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ​which ​places ‌the ‌name in ‌Tier ‌2.

​The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

​- ​**h** ‌→ **H** ​— ​Same, ​capitalized
‌- **a** ​→ ​**a** ​— ‌Same
- ​**o** ‌→ ​**o** ‌— Same
​- ‌**m** ‌→ ​**m** — ​Same
​- ​**a** ‌→ **a** ‌— ​Same

sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/haoma/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**haoma** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Haoma.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"haoma" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Haoma".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"haoma" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Haoma" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Haoma was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Haoma ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Haoma ‌place ​sacred plant, ​immortality ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

### ‌Origins ​(Myth)

‌Haoma appears ​in ‌zoroastrian tradition ​as ​sacred ​plant, immortality. ​The ​name's meaning, ‌"The ​pressed ‌one", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ‌this ​figure.

### ‌Worship ​and Memory ​(Cult)

‌Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ​preserved Haoma ​in ‌ritual, ​text, and ​iconography, ‌ensuring the ​name ​survived ‌into the ​modern ‌scholarly ​record.

The ​myths ​of Haoma ​survive ‌in ‌fragments, summaries, ​and ‌later retellings. ​Each ​version ‌reflects the ‌interests ‌of its ‌tellers ​— ‌poets, priests, ​philosophers, ​and scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; ​it gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Haoma ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Haoma ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Zoroastrian ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming 𐬵𐬀𐬊𐬨𐬀, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to sacred ​plant ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Haoma is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​sacred ​Plant, ‌Immortality ​in the ​mind ‌and ​to ‌ask ​what of ‌it ​endures. ​The ​name means ​"The ​pressed ‌one" ​— and ‌a ​name ‌that ​carries its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly ​invites meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as sacred ‌Plant, ​Immortality ​· ‌The pressed ​one.

‌Sit ​with ​the restored ​form ​— ‌Haoma ‌— and ​the ‌diacritics ​themselves ​become ‌the practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, ​a refusal ‌to ​let ​the ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*haoma* ​stand ​in for ‌the ​whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
